question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act substituted the words ‘armed rebellion’ for ‘internal disturbance’ in National Emergency?
solution:
The correct answer is the** __44th Constitutional Amendment Act,1978__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• National Emergency:

 
 
• Article 352 states that the President can proclaim an Emergency if he/she believes that a “grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion” only on the written recommendation of the cabinet.
 
 
• The 44th Constitutional Amendment of India replaced the term ‘internal disturbance’ with ‘armed rebellion’. *Hence option 2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• Every such proclamation must be laid before the Parliament and it ceases to be in operation unless it is approved by the resolutions of both houses of the parliament with a special majority within one month from the date of issue.
 
• The proclamation of emergency under article 352 can be made in respect of the whole of India or only a part thereof.
 
• During an emergency under article 352, the center has no power to suspend the state government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Under the emergency of Article 352, parliament can legislate in respect of state subjects only by itself.

 
• Anti Defection Law was inserted in the Constitution in 1985 through the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is also called as ‘Mini Constitution’.
 
 
• 42nd Amendment Act added the words ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’ to the preamble.
 
• Through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 10 Fundamental Duties were added upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act transferred five subjects to Concurrent List from State List, that is, (a) education, (b) forests, (c) weights and measures, (d) protection of wild animals and birds, and (e) administration of justice.
